# First cycle: Handle missing values and categorical encoding
# Create copies for processing
train_cycle1 = train_processed.copy()
test_cycle1 = test_processed.copy()

print("=== CYCLE 1: Initial Data Scan ===")

# Check missing values
print("\nMissing values in train set:")
print(train_cycle1.isnull().sum())

print("\nMissing values in test set:")
print(test_cycle1.isnull().sum())

# Handle missing values for numerical columns (excluding label)
numerical_cols = ['age', 'income', 'years_experience', 'credit_score', 'transaction_amount']
for col in numerical_cols:
    if col in train_cycle1.columns:
        # Fill with median for train, then use same median for test
        train_median = train_cycle1[col].median()
        train_cycle1[col] = train_cycle1[col].fillna(train_median)
        test_cycle1[col] = test_cycle1[col].fillna(train_median)
        print(f"Filled missing {col} with median: {train_median:.2f}")

# Handle missing values for binary column 'has_loan'
if 'has_loan' in train_cycle1.columns:
    train_mode = train_cycle1['has_loan'].mode()[0]
    train_cycle1['has_loan'] = train_cycle1['has_loan'].fillna(train_mode)
    test_cycle1['has_loan'] = test_cycle1['has_loan'].fillna(train_mode)
    print(f"Filled missing has_loan with mode: {train_mode}")

# Handle categorical columns with missing values
categorical_cols = ['education', 'employment_status', 'last_payment_date']
for col in categorical_cols:
    if col in train_cycle1.columns:
        # Fill with most frequent category for train, then use same for test
        train_mode = train_cycle1[col].mode()[0] if not train_cycle1[col].mode().empty else 'Unknown'
        train_cycle1[col] = train_cycle1[col].fillna(train_mode)
        test_cycle1[col] = test_cycle1[col].fillna(train_mode)
        print(f"Filled missing {col} with mode: {train_mode}")

# Apply label encoding for categorical columns (alternative to one-hot)
from sklearn.preprocessing import LabelEncoder

label_encoders = {}
for col in ['education', 'employment_status']:
    if col in train_cycle1.columns:
        le = LabelEncoder()
        # Fit on train data only, then transform both train and test
        le.fit(train_cycle1[col])
        train_cycle1[col] = le.transform(train_cycle1[col])
        test_cycle1[col] = le.transform(test_cycle1[col])
        label_encoders[col] = le
        print(f"Label encoded {col} with {len(le.classes_)} unique values")

# Check for remaining issues
print("\n=== After Cycle 1 ===")
print("Missing values in train set:")
print(train_cycle1.isnull().sum())

print("\nMissing values in test set:")
print(test_cycle1.isnull().sum())

print("\nData types after encoding:")
print(train_cycle1.dtypes)
